title: How do you make a net of an octahedron?
description: An octahedron is two square pyramids joined at their square bases. The board unfolds each pyramid's four triangles as a fan, joins the two fans along one edge, and counts the faces, edges and vertices. Keeko's doubt is that the octahedron has ten faces.
teaching_notes: One idea: unfold each pyramid as a fan of four triangles and join the fans along one edge; only the outside surfaces are faces. Watch for students who count the glued square bases as faces.

source: An octahedron is two square pyramids joined at their square
video_script.why: The child plans the net of an octahedron by unfolding each pyramid and joining the parts along an edge, then counts faces, edges and vertices on the outside of the solid.
video_script.substitution: two fans of 4 triangles joined along one edge of the square; 4 + 4 = 8 faces; 4 + 4 + 4 = 12 edges; 4 + 1 + 1 = 6 vertices.
video_script.anchor: the octahedron of the book, two square pyramids joined at their square bases, unfolded into two fans
video_script.wrong_answer: each pyramid has five faces, so the octahedron has ten faces
video_script.wrong_move: Keeko counts the two square bases as faces; they are glued together inside the solid and cannot be touched from outside, so the doubt is struck.
video_script.payoff_line: The net is two fans of four triangles, with eight faces, twelve edges and six vertices

final_answer.value: Two fans of 4 equilateral triangles joined along one edge; 8 faces, 12 edges and 6 vertices
final_answer.spoken: two fans of four equilateral triangles joined along one edge, with eight faces, twelve edges and six vertices

hold_back: Two fans of 4 equilateral triangles joined along one edge; 8 faces, 12 edges and 6 vertices
maths_rules: each square pyramid has 4 triangle faces round its tip; the two square bases are glued together inside
net: a fan of 4 triangles round the top corner and a fan of 4 round the bottom corner, joined along one edge of the square, with no overlap
edges: 4 round the square, 4 up to the top, 4 down to the bottom: 4 + 4 + 4 = 12
vertices: 4 on the square, the top and the bottom: 4 + 1 + 1 = 6
wrong idea: 5 + 5 = 10 counts the glued square bases, which are inside
video_script.design: One idea: unfold each pyramid as a fan and join the fans along one edge. The octahedron opens on the stage; the glued squares are shown inside, out of the count.

narration: <bookmark mark='book'/>This is a question from your book about an octahedron.
<bookmark mark='octa'/>An octahedron means a solid made of two square pyramids joined at their square bases.
<bookmark mark='net'/>A net means a flat shape that folds into the solid.
<bookmark mark='ask'/>Plan a net with triangles whose sides are all equal, and count the faces, edges and vertices.

<bookmark mark='eight'/>Four plus four makes eight faces in all.
<bookmark mark='fans'/>Unfold the top four as a fan round the top corner. Unfold the bottom four as a fan round the bottom corner.

narration: <bookmark mark='square'/>Step three, count the edges. Four edges go round the square.
<bookmark mark='updown'/>Four go up to the top, and four go down to the bottom.
<bookmark mark='sum'/>Four plus four plus four makes twelve edges.

<bookmark mark='sum'/>Four plus one plus one makes six vertices.

beats.on_screen: Answer: two fans of 4 equilateral triangles joined along one edge; 8 faces, 12 edges and 6 vertices

narration: <bookmark mark='ans'/>The net is two fans of four triangles, with eight faces, twelve edges and six vertices.

narration: <bookmark mark='doubt'/>Keeko thinks each pyramid has five faces, so the octahedron has ten faces.
<bookmark mark='inside'/>But the two squares are glued together inside. Nobody can touch them from outside.
<bookmark mark='fix'/>A face must be on the outside, so the squares do not count.
